results.title: Stable polynomials
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A complex multivariate polynomial is stable if it has no zero when every variable lies in the open upper half-plane.

results.title: Real stable polynomials
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A complex multivariate polynomial is real stable if it is stable and has real coefficients.

results.title: Univariate specialization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $p$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, and let $i \in \sigma$ and $x : \sigma \to R$. The univariate specialization of $p$ at $i$ and $x$ is the polynomial in $R[X]$ obtained from $p$ by substituting $X$ for $X_i$ and the constant $x_j$ for every $X_j$ with $j \ne i$; the value $x_i$ is not used.

results.title: Partial derivatives under univariate specialization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $p$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$ and $x : \sigma \to R$, and for a polynomial $q$ write $q_{i,x} \in R[X]$ for its univariate specialization that keeps $X_i$ as the variable $X$ and sets every other $X_j$ to $x_j$. Then $(\partial p / \partial X_i)_{i,x} = (p_{i,x})'$, the derivative of $p_{i,x}$.

results.title: Evaluating a univariate specialization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $p$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, and let $i \in \sigma$, $x : \sigma \to R$ and $t \in R$. Evaluating at $t$ the univariate specialization of $p$ that keeps $X_i$ as the variable and sets every other $X_j$ to $x_j$ gives $p(y)$, where $y_i = t$ and $y_j = x_j$ for $j \ne i$.

results.title: Univariate specialization at real values preserves real coefficients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a complex multivariate polynomial with real coefficients in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and let $a : \sigma \to \mathbb{C}$ with $a_j$ real for every $j \ne i$. Then the univariate specialization of $p$ that keeps $X_i$ as the variable and sets every other $X_j$ to $a_j$ has real coefficients.

results.title: Roots of specializations of stable polynomials lie in the closed lower half-plane
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and let $a : \sigma \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Im} a_j \ge 0$ for every $j \ne i$. If the univariate specialization of $p$ that keeps $X_i$ as the variable and sets every other $X_j$ to $a_j$ is nonzero, then every root $w$ of it satisfies $\operatorname{Im} w \le 0$.

results.title: Subtracting a partial derivative preserves stability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_i p$ for the partial derivative of $p$ with respect to $X_i$. Then $p - \partial_i p$ is stable.

results.title: Subtracting a partial derivative preserves real stability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a real stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_i p$ for the partial derivative of $p$ with respect to $X_i$. Then $p - \partial_i p$ is real stable.

results.title: The mixed differential preserves stability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_s$ indexed by $s \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_s$ for the partial derivative with respect to $X_s$. For every finite list $(i_1, \dots, i_k)$ of indices in $\sigma$ (repetitions allowed, possibly empty), the mixed differential of $p$ along the list, $(1 - \partial_{i_k}) \cdots (1 - \partial_{i_1})\, p$, is stable.

results.title: The mixed differential preserves real stability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a real stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_s$ indexed by $s \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_s$ for the partial derivative with respect to $X_s$. For every finite list $(i_1, \dots, i_k)$ of indices in $\sigma$ (repetitions allowed, possibly empty), the mixed differential of $p$ along the list, $(1 - \partial_{i_k}) \cdots (1 - \partial_{i_1})\, p$, is real stable.

results.title: Real cyclotomic polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the real cyclotomic polynomial $\psi_n \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is the minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}$ of the complex number $\zeta + \zeta^{-1}$, where $\zeta = e^{2\pi i/n}$; for $n \ge 1$ this number is $2\cos(2\pi/n)$.

results.title: Lehmer's identity for the real cyclotomic polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n > 2$ be a natural number, let $\psi_n$ be the real cyclotomic polynomial, let $\Phi_n \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial, and let $\varphi$ be Euler's totient function. Then in the ring $\mathbb{Z}[x, x^{-1}]$ of Laurent polynomials over $\mathbb{Z}$, $x^{\varphi(n)/2} \, \psi_n(x + x^{-1}) = \Phi_n(x)$, that is, $\psi_n(x + x^{-1}) = x^{-\varphi(n)/2} \, \Phi_n(x)$.

results.title: The real cyclotomic polynomial is the minimal polynomial of $\zeta + \zeta^{-1}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $n > 2$ be a natural number, and let $\zeta \in K$ be a primitive $n$-th root of unity. Then the real cyclotomic polynomial $\psi_n$ equals the minimal polynomial of $\zeta + \zeta^{-1}$ over $\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Binary strings
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, a binary string of length $n$ is a function from $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ to $\{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$, that is, a sequence of $n$ bits listed in order.

results.title: Pairs of binary strings
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, a pair of binary strings of length $n$ is an ordered pair $(x, y)$ of binary strings $x$ and $y$, each of length $n$. These pairs form the finite sample space over which expected longest common subsequence lengths are taken.

results.title: Common subsequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For binary strings $x$ and $y$ of length $n$, a finite sequence of bits $z$ is a common subsequence of $x$ and $y$ if $z$ is obtained both from $x$ and from $y$ by deleting some (possibly no) entries and keeping the remaining entries in order.

results.title: Lengths of common subsequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For binary strings $x$ and $y$ of length $n$, the set of natural numbers $k$ such that some binary list of length $k$ is a common subsequence of $x$ and $y$.

results.title: Length of a longest common subsequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For binary strings $x$ and $y$ of length $n$, $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$ is the length returned by the dynamic-programming algorithm for the longest common subsequence, applied to $x$ and $y$ read as lists of bits.

results.title: The LCS length is the maximum common-subsequence length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For binary strings $x$ and $y$ of length $n$, let $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$ be the length returned by the dynamic-programming algorithm for the longest common subsequence on $x$ and $y$. Then some common subsequence of $x$ and $y$ has length $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$, and every common subsequence of $x$ and $y$ has length at most $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$.

results.title: Existence of a longest common subsequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For binary strings $x$ and $y$ of length $n$, there is a binary list $z$ that is a common subsequence of $x$ and $y$, whose length equals the LCS length of $x$ and $y$, and such that every common subsequence $w$ of $x$ and $y$ has length at most the length of $z$.

results.title: The LCS length is at most the string length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For binary strings $x$ and $y$ of length $n$, the length $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$ of a longest common subsequence satisfies $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y) \le n$.

results.title: The LCS length as a bounded maximum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For binary strings $x$ and $y$ of length $n$, the length $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$ of a longest common subsequence equals the largest $k \le n$ such that $x$ and $y$ have a common subsequence of length $k$ (such $k$ exist, since the empty sequence is a common subsequence).

results.title: The finite set of pairs of binary strings

results.title: Expected length of a longest common subsequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the expected LCS length $E_n$ is the average of $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$, the length of a longest common subsequence of $x$ and $y$, over all ordered pairs $(x, y)$ of binary strings of length $n$: it is the sum of $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$ over these pairs divided by their number $4^n$. Equivalently, $E_n$ is the expectation of $\mathrm{LCS}(x, y)$ for two independent uniformly random binary strings…

results.title: Expected LCS length is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$, the expected length of a longest common subsequence of two independent uniformly random binary strings of length $n$ is at least $0$.

results.title: Expected LCS length is at most the string length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$, the expected length of a longest common subsequence of two independent uniformly random binary strings of length $n$ is at most $n$.

results.title: Normalized expected LCS length

results.title: Binary Chvátal–Sankoff constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L_n$ be the length of a longest common subsequence of two independent uniformly random binary strings of length $n$. The binary Chvátal–Sankoff constant is the real number $\liminf_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{E}[L_n]/n$.

results.summary: Let $L_n$ be the length of a longest common subsequence of two independent uniformly random binary strings of length $n$. The notation $C_{31a}$ stands for the binary Chvátal–Sankoff constant $\liminf_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{E}[L_n]/n$.

results.title: Statement of the Chvátal–Sankoff limit theorem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $L_n$ be the length of a longest common subsequence of two independent uniformly random binary strings of length $n$. This proposition asserts that the sequence $\mathbb{E}[L_n]/n$ converges to a real number as $n \to \infty$. Chvátal and Sankoff proved that it holds.

results.title: Trivial bounds for the binary Chvátal–Sankoff constant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L_n$ be the length of a longest common subsequence of two independent uniformly random binary strings of length $n$, and let $C_{31a} = \liminf_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{E}[L_n]/n$ be the binary Chvátal–Sankoff constant. Then $0 \le C_{31a} \le 1$.

results.title: Trivial upper bound for the binary Chvátal–Sankoff constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $C_{31a}$ be the binary Chvátal–Sankoff constant: the limit inferior as $n \to \infty$ of $E_n / n$, where $E_n$ is the expected length of a longest common subsequence of two independent uniformly random binary strings of length $n$. This is the proposition $C_{31a} \le 1$.

results.title: Statement of the Dančík–Paterson upper bound

results.title: Statement of Lueker's upper bound

results.title: Statement of the trivial lower bound

results.title: Statement of the Chvátal–Sankoff positivity bound

results.title: Statement of Lueker's lower bound

results.title: Statement of the Heineman et al. lower bound

results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: For a dimension $d$, a ball tree over the integer points $\mathbb{Z}^d$ (functions $\{0, \dots, d-1\} \to \mathbb{Z}$) is either empty, a leaf holding one point, or a node holding a center point $c \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, a natural number $b$ (the squared-radius bound of the node's sphere) and two child ball trees.

results.title: Accumulating traversal of a ball tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a ball tree $T$ and a list $A$ of points, the accumulating traversal returns $A$ when $T$ is empty, the point $p$ followed by $A$ when $T$ is a leaf holding $p$, and, when $T$ is a node with children $L$ and $R$, the accumulating traversal of $L$ whose accumulator is the accumulating traversal of $R$ with accumulator $A$.

results.title: Point list of a ball tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The point list of a ball tree is the list of the points held at its leaves, from left to right: the empty tree gives the empty list, a leaf holding $p$ gives the list $[p]$, and a node gives the point list of its left subtree followed by the point list of its right subtree. The centers stored at nodes are not included.

results.title: Size of a ball tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The size of a ball tree is the number of points held in its leaves: it is $0$ for the empty tree, $1$ for a leaf, and the sum of the sizes of the two children for a node; the center of a node is not counted.

results.title: Number of points of a ball tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every ball tree $t$, the list of points stored in $t$, read from left to right, has length equal to the size of $t$.

results.title: Squared Euclidean distance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For points $p, q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the squared distance from $p$ to $q$ is the natural number $\sum_{i=0}^{d-1} (p_i - q_i)^2$, computed in $\mathbb{Z}$ and then converted to $\mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Symmetry of squared distance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all points $p, q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the squared distance from $p$ to $q$ equals the squared distance from $q$ to $p$.

results.title: Relaxed triangle inequality for squared distance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all points $a, b, c \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, writing $\delta(x, y)$ for the squared distance from $x$ to $y$, we have $\delta(a, c) \le 2\,(\delta(a, b) + \delta(b, c))$.

results.title: Squared covering radius
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a center $c \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and a list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the squared covering radius of $P$ about $c$ is the largest squared distance from $c$ to a point of $P$, or $0$ if $P$ is empty.

results.title: Points lie within the squared radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and let $L$ be a list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$. For every point $p$ of $L$, the squared distance from $c$ to $p$ is at most the squared radius of $L$ around $c$, the largest squared distance from $c$ to a point of $L$.

results.title: Ball-tree similarity search
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The search of a ball tree $T$ for a query point $q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and a squared radius $r \in \mathbb{N}$ is the accumulating search of $T$ for $q$ and $r$ started with the empty accumulator.

results.title: Bounding-sphere invariant of a ball tree
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Validity of a ball tree is defined inductively: the empty tree and every leaf are valid, and a node with center $c$ and squared-radius bound $b$ is valid when both of its subtrees are valid and every point in the point list of either subtree lies within squared Euclidean distance $b$ of $c$.

results.title: Ball-tree search is exact
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every ball tree $T$ over $\mathbb{Z}^d$ satisfying the bounding-sphere invariant, every query point $q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and every $r \in \mathbb{N}$, the search of $T$ for $q$ and $r$ equals the list of points of $T$, from left to right, filtered to the points $p$ whose squared distance from $q$ is at most $r$, in their order. Pruning against the bounding spheres loses no point.

results.title: Search of a valid ball tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a ball tree satisfying the bounding-sphere invariant. For all $q, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and every natural number $r$, $p$ is returned by the similarity search of $t$ with query $q$ and squared radius $r$ if and only if $p$ is one of the points stored in $t$ and the squared distance from $q$ to $p$ is at most $r$.

results.title: Ball trees built by halving are valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the ball tree built from it by recursive halving satisfies the bounding-sphere invariant.

results.title: A built ball tree stores a permutation of its input
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the list of points of the ball tree built from $P$, from left to right, is a permutation of $P$.

results.title: Points of a built ball tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $L$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and every point $p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, $p$ is one of the points stored in the ball tree built from $L$ if and only if $p$ occurs in $L$.

results.title: Size of a built ball tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the size of the ball tree built from $P$ equals the length of $P$, that is, the number of entries of $P$ counted with repetition.

results.title: Ball-tree search of a built tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, every query point $q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and every $r \in \mathbb{N}$, let $T$ be the ball tree built from $P$. The search of $T$ for $q$ and $r$ equals the list of points of $T$, from left to right, filtered to the points $p$ whose squared distance from $q$ is at most $r$, in their order.

results.title: Ball-tree search of a built tree, up to order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, every query point $q \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and every $r \in \mathbb{N}$, the search of the ball tree built from $P$ for $q$ and $r$ is a permutation of the sublist of $P$ consisting of the points $p$ whose squared distance from $q$ is at most $r$, kept with their multiplicities.

results.title: Search of a built ball tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, let $q, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and let $r$ be a natural number. Then $p$ is returned by the similarity search with query $q$ and squared radius $r$ on the ball tree built from $L$ if and only if $p$ occurs in $L$ and the squared distance from $q$ to $p$ is at most $r$.
